_meta.description: Curated offline biomedical evidence for key Ayurvedic herbs/formulations. Used as fallback when PubMed E-utilities are unavailable or rate-limited.

entries.title: An investigation into the stress-relieving and pharmacological actions of an ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) extract: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
entries.abstract_snippet: A standardized root extract of Withania somnifera (300 mg twice daily) significantly reduced perceived stress and cortisol levels in a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial over 60 days. Participants showed improvements in sleep quality and overall well-being scores.

entries.title: Efficacy and safety of Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) root extract in improving sexual function in women
entries.abstract_snippet: Ashwagandha root extract (300 mg twice daily for 8 weeks) significantly improved sexual function scores, arousal, lubrication, orgasm, and satisfaction in women, consistent with its classical Vajikarna (aphrodisiac) and Balya (strength-promoting) indications.

entries.title: Curcumin: A Review of Its Effects on Human Health
entries.abstract_snippet: Curcumin from Curcuma longa modulates inflammatory signaling (NF-κB, COX-2), exhibits antioxidant and chemopreventive properties, and shows clinical benefit in metabolic syndrome, arthritis, and anxiety. Its poor bioavailability is enhanced by piperine co-administration.

entries.title: Sesame and its lignans: pharmacological effects and clinical applications
entries.abstract_snippet: Sesamin and sesamolin from Sesamum indicum exhibit significant anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and chondroprotective properties. Clinical studies support topical sesame oil application (Abhyanga) for reducing joint stiffness and alleviating Vata-predominant musculoskeletal conditions.

entries.title: Triphala: A comprehensive Ayurvedic review of bioactivity, therapeutic uses, and safety
entries.journal: Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine
entries.abstract_snippet: Triphala (Emblica officinalis, Terminalia chebula, Terminalia bellirica) exhibits prebiotic gut-microbiome modulation, antioxidant activity, and mild prokinetic (Anulomana) properties without stimulant-laxative dependence. Supported in Ayurveda for Rasayana and Tridosha balancing.

entries.title: Cow ghee (clarified butter) and its effect on brain and metabolic health: A review
entries.abstract_snippet: Ghrita (clarified cow's ghee) is rich in butyric acid and conjugated linoleic acid, supporting colonocyte metabolism and blood-brain barrier integrity. It acts as a lipophilic carrier enhancing bioavailability of fat-soluble phytocompounds consistent with Ayurvedic Medhya Rasayana use.

entries.title: Bacopa monnieri in cognitive enhancement: A systematic review of RCTs
entries.abstract_snippet: Bacopa monnieri (Brahmi) supplementation over 12 weeks significantly improved memory acquisition, retention, and processing speed in healthy adults and cognitively impaired elderly, supporting its classical Medhya (intellect-promoting) Rasayana designation in Charaka Samhita.

entries.title: Boswellia serrata, a potential anti-inflammatory agent: an overview
entries.abstract_snippet: Boswellia serrata (Shallaki) resin contains boswellic acids (AKBA) that selectively inhibit 5-lipoxygenase, reducing leukotriene synthesis. Clinical trials show efficacy in osteoarthritis and inflammatory bowel disease, consistent with Ayurvedic Sandhi-vata (joint pain) indications.

entries.title: Neem (Azadirachta indica): A tree for solving global problems
entries.abstract_snippet: Azadirachta indica (Nimba) exhibits broad-spectrum antimicrobial, antifungal, anti-inflammatory, and antidiabetic properties. Active compounds include nimbin and azadirachtin. Classical Ayurvedic use for Kushtha (skin disorders), Prameha (diabetes), and Kandughna (anti-pruritic) is well-supported.

entries.title: Guduchi (Tinospora cordifolia): A Review of Its Immunomodulatory and Anti-inflammatory Properties
entries.abstract_snippet: Tinospora cordifolia (Guduchi/Giloy) contains berberine, tinosporine, and polysaccharides that enhance macrophage phagocytosis, NK cell activity, and suppress TNF-α. It is classified as Rasayana and Vayasthapana (age-stabilizing) in Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana.

entries.title: Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus) in female reproductive health: Systematic evidence review
entries.abstract_snippet: Asparagus racemosus (Shatavari) demonstrates estrogenic, galactagogue, and adaptogenic effects in clinical studies. Steroidal saponins (shatavarins) support female reproductive health and lactation, consistent with its classical role as the supreme Stanyajanana (milk-promoting) and Garbhasthapana herb.

entries.title: Moringa oleifera (Shigru): Nutritional composition and pharmacological activities review
entries.abstract_snippet: Moringa oleifera (Shigru) leaves contain isothiocyanates, flavonoids, and polyunsaturated fatty acids with demonstrated anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, and antidiabetic activity. Rich in bioavailable iron, relevant to classical Panduroga (anaemia) indication.
